name: Sham (no field)
origin: Standard double-blind sham control, as used by Granqvist et al. 2005 and in sham-helmet studies by van Elk and colleagues
summary: Zero output with identical timers and relay behaviour, for blinded comparisons. Prefer the "Blind" option, which picks real or sham at random for any preset.
notes: Sham, never-energized 'God helmets' produce extraordinary experiences in some people (a minority in the earlier studies, by the lead author's account); absorption predicted how often and how strongly they came (Maij & van Elk 2018), and self-identified spirituality predicted them in a pre-registered festival study of 193 people (Maij, van Elk & Schjoedt 2019). In Granqvist 2005 (double-blind, 89 people) suggestibility, not the field, predicted sensed presence and mystical experiences. A sham only helps if you can't tell it from the real session: keep the room, instructions and timing identical, record your ratings before unblinding, and note which arm you guessed. If you can hear coil hum in the real session, mask it in both arms. Unpleasant feelings can come from the setting alone; stop on distress.
setting: Identical to the program it is compared with.
schedule: Decide the outcome measure in advance; at least two real and two sham sessions in counterbalanced order, at least 24 h apart.
source: Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ (suggestibility, not the field, predicted experiences) ; Maij & van Elk 2018, Conscious Cogn 66:1 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30355534/ ; Maij, van Elk & Schjoedt 2019, Religion Brain Behav 9:108 https://doi.org/10.1080/2153599x.2017.1403952 ; Thomas et al. 2007 (silent identical sham headsets) https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2670735/
